Qisland bundles vendored copies of TWO third-party components (details below).

================================================================
[2] lunar-javascript — 每日宜忌通书数据表
Upstream: https://github.com/6tail/lunar-javascript  (v1.7.7)
License:  MIT (see LICENSE-MIT-lunar.txt in this folder)
Files:    huangli_data.h
            - LunarUtil.YI_JI       141 词条，用 zh-CN i18n 表还原为中文
            - LunarUtil.DAY_YI_JI   34,149 字符编码表
            - LunarUtil.SHEN_SHA[0] 「无」
          The lookup rules (getDayYi / getDayJi) were re-implemented in
          pure C in src/lunar.c. No JS runtime, no network, no data edits.
          The month pillar must be the SOLAR-TERM month (月建), not the
          lunar month — verified against upstream: 2025-01-29 is 丁丑月,
          not 戊寅月.

================================================================
[1] lunar-calendar  —— 本地农历 / 24 节气库

  lunar-calendar  —  Chinese lunar date and 24 solar terms implemented with C
  Upstream: https://github.com/iseemoon/lunar-calendar
  License:  Apache License, Version 2.0 (see LICENSE in this folder)
  Files:    lunar_date.c / lunar_date.h / solar_term.c / solar_term.h (Apache-2.0)

Modifications made to [1] for Qisland (no data tables were changed):
  1. lunar_date.c  : #include "date.h" -> "lunar_date.h"
                     (upstream ships the header under a different name)
  2. lunar_date.h  : added <stdint.h> for int32_t / uint8_t
  3. solar_term.h  : #include "date.h" -> "lunar_date.h"
  4. solar_term.c  : declared the SOLAR_TERM_TIMES lookup pointer const
                     (silences -Wdiscarded-qualifiers under -Wall -Wextra)
  5. All four files got a short header comment noting these changes.
  6. Renamed the library's `DATE` struct to `LUNAR_DATE` (all four files).
     Windows wtypes.h already defines `DATE` as `double`; without this the
     MinGW build fails with "conflicting types for DATE".
  7. solar_term.c: replaced localtime() with fixed UTC+8 integer conversion
     in get_day_of_solar_term(). Upstream derived the solar-term calendar
     day from the process's local timezone, which is wrong for the Chinese
     calendar (defined on UTC+8) and breaks for pre-1970 dates on Windows
     CRT. Example: 2026 冬至 is UTC 2026-12-21 20:49 = 2026-12-22 in UTC+8.
     No data tables were touched, only the timestamp -> y/m/d conversion.

  7b. FIX to patch 7: the first version of that conversion forgot the
     +719468 epoch shift. Hinnant civil_from_days counts days from
     0000-03-01, while Unix epoch days count from 1970-01-01. Without the
     shift every solar term came out in year 0056, so ALL 24 terms looked
     "already passed": the date card showed 「距小寒0天」 for 2026-11-18,
     the month pillar collapsed to 子月 (庚子月) all year, and the yi/ji
     lookup used the wrong month. Verified full 2026 term list after the
     fix: 小寒 01-05 ... 立冬 11-07 / 小雪 11-22 / 冬至 12-22.
  8. Added two local #pragma GCC diagnostic ignored lines in lunar_date.h
     for -Wsign-compare / -Wold-style-declaration, which upstream triggers.
     Project code is still compiled with -Wall -Wextra fully enabled.

Coverage: solar years 1900..2099 (lunar-year tables run 1887..2111).
The 24 solar terms are stored as exact UTC millisecond timestamps for every
year, not approximated by a formula. All strings are UTF-8; Qisland converts
them to wide strings at the boundary in src/lunar.c.

No network access, no threads, no allocations, no files, no Win7 update
requirement. Compiled directly into Qisland.exe.
